# Media Protection Standard

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes requirements for the protection of system media containing Acme Health information throughout its lifecycle, from creation through disposal. This standard addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines [NIST 800-53 MP-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-1 High | ARC-AMPE MP-1].

This standard must be structured at the organization level [ARC-AMPE MP-1].

This standard facilitates the implementation of media protection policies and associated media protection controls [NIST 800-53 MP-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-1 High | ARC-AMPE MP-1].

This standard shall be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)].

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

Acme Health shall designate [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the media protection policy and procedures [NIST 800-53 MP-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-1 High].

Acme Health shall designate organization-defined officials to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the media protection policy and procedures [ARC-AMPE MP-1].

## 3. Policy and Procedure Development and Maintenance

### 3.1 Policy and Procedure Review

Acme Health shall review and update the media protection policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events] [NIST 800-53 MP-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-1 High].

Acme Health shall review and update the media protection procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events] [NIST 800-53 MP-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-1 High].

Acme Health shall review and update the media protection policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events [ARC-AMPE MP-1].

Acme Health shall review and update the media protection procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events [ARC-AMPE MP-1].

### 3.2 Documentation Requirements

Acme Health shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)].

Acme Health shall retain documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)].

Acme Health shall make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii)].

Acme Health shall review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii)].

## 4. Hardware and Electronic Media Controls

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media that contain electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(1)].

Acme Health shall maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(iii)].

Acme Health shall create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information, when needed, before movement of equipment [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(iv)].

## 5. Media Access Control

### 5.1 Access Restrictions

Acme Health shall restrict access to [Assignment: organization-defined types of digital and/or non-digital media] to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] [NIST 800-53 MP-2 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-2 High].

Acme Health shall restrict access to all types of digital and non-digital media to organization-defined personnel or roles, in compliance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization [ARC-AMPE MP-2].

Acme Health shall disable CD/DVD writers and only allow access to CD/DVD viewing and downloading capabilities to authorized individuals with a valid need to know [ARC-AMPE MP-2].

Acme Health shall disable USB ports and only allow access to using USB device capabilities to authorized individuals with a valid need to know [ARC-AMPE MP-2].

### 5.2 Workforce Access Management

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of the workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access from obtaining access to electronic protected health information [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(3)(i)].

Acme Health shall implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(A)].

Acme Health shall implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to electronic protected health information is appropriate [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B)].

Acme Health shall implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends or as required by determinations made regarding appropriate access [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C)].

### 5.3 Workstation Physical Safeguards

Acme Health shall implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information, to restrict access to authorized users [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(c)].

## 6. Media Marking

Acme Health shall mark system media indicating the distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable security markings (if any) of the information [NIST 800-53 MP-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-3 High | ARC-AMPE MP-3].

Acme Health shall exempt [Assignment: organization-defined types of media exempted from marking] from marking if the media remain within [Assignment: organization-defined controlled areas] [NIST 800-53 MP-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-3 High].

Acme Health shall exempt specific types of media or hardware components, as specified, in writing, by the Chief Information Officer (CIO) or their designated representative, from marking if the media remains within a secure environment [ARC-AMPE MP-3].

Media (including removable media) must have, at a minimum, the following markings clearly identifiable by labels or other approved coding systems: Creation Date; Information Safeguarding Markings (based on applicable record retention regulations); and Organization-defined Contact Information (for backup tapes, the system name must be included in addition to all other items) [ARC-AMPE MP-3].

Media containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI), or the container for the media if labeling the media is not practicable, must be marked appropriately and consistent with ACA record retention regulations [ARC-AMPE MP-3].

## 7. Media Storage

### 7.1 Physical Control and Secure Storage

Acme Health shall physically control and securely store [Assignment: organization-defined types of digital and/or non-digital media] within [Assignment: organization-defined controlled areas] [NIST 800-53 MP-4 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-4 High].

Acme Health shall physically control and securely store all magnetic tapes, external removable hard drives, flash/thumb drives, diskettes, compact disks, and digital video disks within organization-defined controlled areas [ARC-AMPE MP-4].

Acme Health shall protect system media types defined in the media storage control until the media are destroyed or sanitized using approved equipment, techniques, and procedures [NIST 800-53 MP-4 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-4 High | ARC-AMPE MP-4].

### 7.2 Storage Protection Methods

Acme Health shall encrypt digital media via the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards [ARC-AMPE MP-4].

Acme Health shall protect non-digital media in secure storage in locked cabinets or safes [ARC-AMPE MP-4].

Acme Health shall store removable media that contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in a securable area or in a locked container [ARC-AMPE MP-4].

If PII is recorded on magnetic media with other data, Acme Health shall protect the media as if all the data contains PII [ARC-AMPE MP-4].

### 7.3 Media Storage Area Access

Acme Health shall restrict access to media storage areas and log access attempts and access granted using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] [NIST 800-53 MP-4(2)].

## 8. Media Transport

### 8.1 Protection During Transport

Acme Health shall protect and control [Assignment: organization-defined types of system media] during transport outside of controlled areas using [Assignment: organization-defined controls] [NIST 800-53 MP-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-5 High].

Acme Health shall protect and control digital and non-digital media containing sensitive information, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII), during transport outside of controlled areas using organization-defined controls such as: Latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption module; Locked/securable containers or tamper-evident packaging transported via authorized personnel; A trackable receipt by the commercial shipping carrier; and Sealed packing cartons for non-digital media containing sensitive information [ARC-AMPE MP-5].

### 8.2 Accountability and Documentation

Acme Health shall maintain accountability for system media during transport outside of controlled areas [NIST 800-53 MP-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-5 High | ARC-AMPE MP-5].

Acme Health shall document activities associated with the transport of system media [NIST 800-53 MP-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-5 High | ARC-AMPE MP-5].

Acme Health shall restrict the activities associated with the transport of system media to authorized personnel [NIST 800-53 MP-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-5 High | ARC-AMPE MP-5].

### 8.3 Custodial Control

Acme Health shall employ an identified custodian during transport of system media outside of controlled areas [NIST 800-53 MP-5(3)].

## 9. Media Sanitization and Disposal

### 9.1 Final Disposition

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic protected health information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(i)].

Acme Health shall implement procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(d)(2)(ii)].

### 9.2 Sanitization Requirements

Acme Health shall sanitize [Assignment: organization-defined system media] prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse using [Assignment: organization-defined sanitization techniques and procedures] [NIST 800-53 MP-6 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-6 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-6 High].

Acme Health shall sanitize digital and non-digital system media prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse using defined sanitization techniques and procedures in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88 guidelines [ARC-AMPE MP-6].

Acme Health shall employ sanitization mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information [NIST 800-53 MP-6 Low | NIST 800-53 MP-6 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MP-6 High | ARC-AMPE MP-6].

Acme Health shall finely shred hard-copy documents using approved equipment, techniques, and procedures, and employ cross-cut shredding at a minimum [ARC-AMPE MP-6].

Acme Health shall sanitize media containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) prior to disposal, release out of organization, or release for reuse using the latest FIPS-validated media sanitization techniques or procedures [ARC-AMPE MP-6].

Acme Health shall dispose of or sanitize surplus equipment in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization [ARC-AMPE MP-6].

### 9.3 Sanitization Review and Verification

Acme Health shall review, approve, track, document, and verify media sanitization and disposal actions [NIST 800-53 MP-6(1) High | ARC-AMPE MP-6(1)].

Acme Health shall securely destroy or dispose of sensitive information, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII), appropriately and reasonably and per retention schedules [ARC-AMPE MP-6(1)].

Media-related sanitization records must contain the following information: Name of media recipient; Signature of media recipient; Date/time received; Media control number and contents; Movement or routing information; and If disposed of, the date, time, and method of destruction [ARC-AMPE MP-6(1)].

### 9.4 Sanitization Testing and Validation

Acme Health shall test sanitization equipment and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to ensure that the intended sanitization is being achieved [NIST 800-53 MP-6(2) High].

Acme Health shall test sanitization equipment and procedures within every one (1) year to ensure that the organization achieves the intended sanitization [ARC-AMPE MP-6(2)].

### 9.5 Portable Storage Device Sanitization

Acme Health shall apply nondestructive sanitization techniques to portable storage devices prior to connecting such devices to the system under the following circumstances: [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances] [NIST 800-53 MP-6(3) High].

### 9.6 Dual Authorization

Acme Health shall enforce dual authorization for the sanitization of [Assignment: organization-defined system media] [NIST 800-53 MP-6(7)].

### 9.7 Remote Sanitization

Acme Health shall provide the capability to purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components] [Selection: remotely; under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions]] [NIST 800-53 MP-6(8)].

## 10. Data Integrity

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(c)(1)].

Acme Health shall implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(c)(2)].

## 11. Document Administration

This standard is effective upon approval by [Assignment: organization-defined authority] and shall be reviewed and updated in accordance with Section 3.1 of this standard.
